segments.text: Heat stress, a stomach bug, a chemical leak. The first signs rarely show up in one dataset. A few extra clinic visits, some sick days, a couple of incident reports. Reviewed separately, nobody connects them until the problem has grown. This is Prodrome.

Prodrome watches clinic visits, lab results, sickness absence, incident reports, and real heat and air quality, district by district. It learns what normal looks like given the weather, so a hot week alone doesn't set it off. Here, in Al Ain Industrial, incident reports are running two and a half times what's expected, and heat illness visits nearly three times. Two different signals, agreeing. That opens an alert.

And it shows its working: which signals drove the alert, observed versus expected, and how much the weather already explains. The response is proportionate. A watch, then an advisory, then action on day three, restricting outdoor work hours, with the responsible role named. Not a person, not an employer. A district, a hazard, and a human who checks.

It also shows its mistakes. This one is a false alarm. We tune to an alert budget of about one false alert a month across the emirate, because an alert that cries wolf gets ignored. A classic three sigma rule would fire nearly ten a month.

On two held out years of simulated outbreaks, with thresholds frozen from the year before, Prodrome caught sixty nine percent of events, and seventy three percent of its alerts were real. A weekly review caught forty four percent, three days later. Heat clusters were the weakest, two out of eight, and we say so.

If data goes missing, it degrades gently. With twenty percent of days missing in every feed, it still catches sixty two percent. If every clinical feed goes dark, it fails silent rather than guess. And a single faulty feed raises an alert only a quarter of the time, versus eighty four percent without cross checking.

Privacy is built in. Only district level aggregates exist. No names, no employers, no coordinates. Small counts are suppressed, and every role gets its own data file. An employer sees weekly bands, a policy analyst monthly trends. Nothing here can be used for individual decisions.

If acting early avoids even thirty percent of what's still ahead, Prodrome averts over four times as many illness visits, incidents and lost workdays as a weekly review, in simulation. And every alert leaves an evidence trail for regulators.
To be clear, the health data is simulated, because none was provided. The weather is real. Prodrome. From signals to action, before the burden grows.
